newsitem.title: COMOROS: OAU and Anjouan secessionists begin talks.
newsitem.headline: OAU and Anjouan secessionists begin talks.

text.p: Secessionist leaders of the breakaway Anjouan island have told the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) that their decision to declare independence from the Islamic Republic of the Comoros was irreversible.
The first round of talks between an OAU delegation and the ruling body of breakaway Anjouan in the Indian Ocean Comoros islands began on Tuesday, officials said on Wednesday.

Islanders on Anjouan, and on the nearby island of Moheli, say they want to return to French rule because they have experienced nothing but poverty and political unrest since independence from France in 1975.

The poverty in the Islamic Republic of the Comoros contrasts with the comparative prosperity on the adjoining island of Mayotte, which voted against independence in 1975 and remains under French rule.
Foundi Abdallah Ibrahim, 75, who led the secession demand, was declared "president" of Anjouan by a crowd of islanders last week.

The secessionists' co-ordination ruling body, led by Ibrahim, say they have rejected the OAU delegation's insistence that they respect the territorial integrity of the Federal Islamic Republic of the Comoros.
"Our independence is irreversible," a secessionist leader told Reuters on Tuesday night.
The leader of the OAU delegation, Pierre Yere late on Tuesday described Anjouan's leaders as "understanding".
"The Anjouan co-ordination has accepted to dialogue with the Moroni authorities and has also committed itself not to undertake anything which would make the tension rise," he said.

The Anjouan co-ordination demanded the withdrawal of troops sent last month by the Comorian authorities to quell pro-secessionist unrest and proposed that eventual talks with the Comorian authorities should take place in Mauritius.
The OAU delegation will go to Moheli island on Wednesday which also wants to secede from the Comorian Federation.
The delegation is then expected on Moroni, the capital of the Comorian Federation to hold talks with Comorian authorities, before heading back to Anjouan later on Wednesday evening.
The opposition umbrella organisation in the Comoros, the Forum of National Recovery (FNR) held a mass rally in Moroni on Tuesday over the secession crisis.
Opposition leaders denounced "the government's inconscience over the seriousness of the situation and the government negligence over the handling of the crisis."
The FNR demanded the resignation of President Taki whom they consider "the grave digger" of the national integrity.
France has refused to support the secessionists, saying the Anjouan situation is serious and could destabilise the whole region.
Three people including a gendarme were killed on July 14 as demonstrators, pressing for Anjouan to return to French rule or be independent, clashed with security forces.
